statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum cardinality of a valid matching M, where a valid matching is a set of pairs (i,j) such that 0 <= i < len(players), 0 <= j < len(trainers), players[i] <= trainers[j], no two pairs in M have the same first component, and no two pairs in M have the same second component. Thus r = max { |M| : M is a valid matching }.
preconditions: 1 <= len(players), len(trainers) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(players), 1 <= players[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(trainers), 1 <= trainers[j] <= 1000000000.

preconditions: 1 <= len(players), len(trainers) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(players), 1 <= players[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(trainers), 1 <= trainers[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let A_1 <= A_2 <= ... <= A_n be the entries of players sorted into nondecreasing order, where n = len(players), and let B_1 <= B_2 <= ... <= B_m be the entries of trainers sorted into nondecreasing order, where m = len(trainers). The function returns a result r, and r is the largest integer k with 0 <= k <= min(n,m) such that for every q with 1 <= q <= k, A_q <= B_{m-k+q}.
